column3: Close to the Hebrew; the four Hebrew locust names are rendered “chewing locust,” “swarming locust,” “crawling locust,” and “consuming locust”; their exact meanings are uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “sweet wine” is rendered “new wine.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a lioness” is rendered “a fierce lion.”
Close to the Hebrew; “my fig tree into a stump” is rendered “ruined My fig tree.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the ground has dried up (mourns)” is rendered “The land mourns.”
Close to the Hebrew; “like devastation” is rendered “as destruction.”
Close to the Hebrew; “under their shovels” is rendered “under the clods,” and “are desolate” “are in shambles”; the rare words are uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “they have suffered” is rendered “suffer punishment.”
